items.title: 22.2 Key statistical measures and their calculation

source_refs.note: Topic 22.2 (PDF 189); an original formula card is added to collect the chapter's formulas.

blocks.text: Key statistical measures summarise data and show its central tendency, variability and distribution. The mean is the average value, the median the middle point and the mode the most frequent value; the standard deviation and range measure spread; and percentiles divide the data into intervals for deeper analysis.

blocks.alt: A card of seven formulas. Mean (ungrouped) = sum of x / n. Mean (grouped) = sum of (f times x) / sum of f. Median = middle value of the ordered data. Mode (grouped) = l + [(fm - f1) / ((fm - f1) + (fm - f2))] times h. Standard deviation sigma = square root of [sum of (x - mu) squared / N]. Range = Xmax - Xmin. Percentile rank R = (P / 100) times (n + 1).
blocks.caption: The key formulas of this chapter (original formula card).
blocks.long_description: The mean of ungrouped data is the sum of the values divided by their number; for grouped data each class midpoint is multiplied by its frequency, the products are added and divided by the total frequency. The median is the middle value of ordered data, or the average of the two middle values when the number of values is even. For grouped data the mode is l + [(fm - f1) / ((fm - f1) + (fm - f2))] x h, where l is the lower boundary of the modal class, fm its frequency, f1 and f2 the frequencies of the classes before and after it, and h the class width. The standard deviation is the square root of the average squared deviation from the mean, the range is the largest value minus the smallest, and the rank of the Pth percentile is (P / 100) x (n + 1).

blocks.title: Reading the formulas in plain words
blocks.text: Mean = sum of values / number of values. Grouped mean = sum of (frequency x midpoint) / sum of frequencies. Range = largest value - smallest value. Percentile rank R = (P / 100) x (n + 1). Standard deviation = square root of [sum of (value - mean) squared / number of values].

blocks.prompt: Which measures describe the centre of data, and which describe its spread?
blocks.explanation: Centre: mean, median and mode. Spread: standard deviation and range (percentiles show the distribution).

items: Spread: standard deviation, range; percentiles split the distribution.
